note: The central PARADOXES and the PUNCTUMS of Ada Research's texts, made into stickers (2026-11-13). Seven readers read the walked prose (final.md), the wall texts and the framework and returned 112 candidates, each quote checked word for word; a truth critic and a sticker critic judged them in context; these 28 were chosen by hand, one per shared tension, across the spine. A paradox is two things a text holds true at once (a, b: the badge's paper and ink halves); a punctum (Barthes) is the detail that pricks (a: the caption under its photograph). 'quote' must stay word for word in 'file' or tools/stickers_seed.ts stops; 'line' is a reader's hint. Drawn by ada_encyclopedia src/lib/sticker-starter.ts (READING_MOTIFS[motif]).

readings.beyond: The museum asking of its own rooms, this one included, what the rails have made harder to think and what continues beyond their reach.

readings.a: WHAT THE BODY KNOWS AND THE BOOK CANNOT YET SAY
readings.quote: Palle's body-side registers (punctum/thrownness, ... the buzz/haptic, 'you are here', small/medium/large) did NOT fall out of ... the corpus — they live in VR and walked prose, not card text. ... the darkest fold: what the body knows and the book cannot yet say.
readings.beyond: A second, hand-named source of registers from walks in the headset, read against the measured matrix; where the two disagree is what the book has yet to learn to say.

readings.a: It fits a hand ... and nothing for a surface that carries a body
